name: Live interview capture
oneLiner: Phone records discovery interviews; whisper transcribes live; insights on demand.
problem: Discovery interviews at a client site produce notes nobody can type fast enough, and the knowledge walks out the door with the interviewer.
solution: Phone records in short standalone takes (iOS-safe), each take posts to a Mac, local whisper transcribes in the client's language, the transcript grows live on every founder's phone. An on-demand local model pass ('what are we missing?') reads transcript + checklist + prep brief mid-interview. Recording hardened with a retry queue so a dropped request never loses audio.
payload:
# Live interview capture — build spec

## Shape
1. Roster page: schedule per day, status chips (scheduled → live → interviewed), driven from a repo/markdown the client-side lead edits.
2. Interview page: sticky timer (amber at 75% of slot), tappable field-card checklist, notes tab, opname tab.
3. Opname: MediaRecorder restarted per ~20s take (iOS Safari cannot produce decodable mid-stream chunks). POST each take → save to disk BEFORE transcription; whisper failure returns 200 + empty text (never resend-and-duplicate). 'Stop' drains queue, concats takes via ffmpeg.
4. Live transcript file per person per day; both phones poll a GET endpoint at 5s.
5. Insight endpoint: local model over transcript + unticked checklist steps + the person's prep questions. On demand only, never auto.

## Pins
- Whisper model: multilingual large-v3-turbo for non-English; letterless output reads as silence.
- Segment files 0600; audio never leaves the machine.
- Wake lock + banner: locking the phone kills the mic.

## Adapt per client
- Roster source (their scheduling truth)
- Field card (their interview script)
- Language for whisper

name: Trend radar
oneLiner: Reads Reddit/TikTok for a product category, ranks keyword momentum, predicts what pops next.
problem: Buyers pick products on gut and licensor decks; by the time a trend is obvious in stores it is too late to order against it.
solution: Fetch agents sweep category subreddits and TikTok (screenshot + vision pass), keyword extraction with category-weighted scoring, memory layer so each analysis builds on the last (no contradicting last week's data point), anomaly detection for out-of-nowhere spikes rather than steady leaders. Feeds a ranked board with per-keyword momentum.
payload:
# Trend radar — build spec

## Stages
1. SOURCES: per category, maintain subreddit list + TikTok hashtag/keyword list. Fetch on schedule.
2. EXTRACT: keyword/entity extraction per post; weight by engagement and category-closeness (a toy-adjacent keyword outranks a generic one).
3. RANK: momentum score per keyword = growth rate × volume × category weight. Keep a ranked feed.
4. ANOMALY PASS: flag keywords whose growth breaks their own trend line — the 'out of nowhere, this thing is on fire' signal, separate from the steady top-10.
5. MEMORY: every analysis stored; next run reads prior context so rankings stay consistent and drift is visible.
6. PREDICT (layer 2): train per-category models on the history; report direction, not certainty.

## Honest limits
- Layer 1 is 'what is hot now'; prediction needs months of history.
- Competitors can buy the same signal; the edge is category tuning + client's own sell-through joined in.

## Adapt per client
- Category keyword seeds and platforms
- Join with their sales data for a 'we should reorder / drop' signal

name: Voice-gated content pipeline
oneLiner: Source → write → deterministic voice lint → on-brand render → human-approved publish.
problem: AI-written content drifts off brand voice, and nobody trusts it enough to post without rereading everything.
solution: Five fixed stages: sources are swept and ranked (RSS + reader, dedupe by URL and title similarity), a writer drafts in the brand voice, a deterministic linter built from the voice guide blocks violations (banned words, hook rules, length band, structure) — errors block approval, one rewrite on failure — renders produce on-brand images/PDF, and publishing is copy-open: a human presses post, always. Feedback memory joins post metrics back into the writer prompt.
payload:
# Voice-gated content pipeline — build spec

## Stages
1. SOURCE: feed list in config; sweep, dedupe (URL match + >80% title trigram similarity), rank.
2. WRITE: one recipe per content type; writer prompt carries voice guide + lessons from past post metrics.
3. GATE: deterministic linter compiled from the client's voice guide — banned words, phantom-source check, hook-inside-N-chars, length band, paragraph/hashtag rules, at-least-one-number. Blocking errors stop approval; exactly one auto-rewrite with violations listed.
4. DESIGN: render templates (image/carousel/PDF) from the draft, brand tokens only.
5. PUBLISH: copy-open flow — copy text, open composer, human posts, 'mark posted' keeps the log honest. Nothing auto-posts.
6. MEMORY: manual metrics entry per post; lessons only surface when both sides of a comparison have n≥2 and gap ≥25%.

## Why it converts
The voice guide becomes testable rules, so trust comes from the gate, not from rereading.

## Adapt per client
- Voice guide → lint rules session with the client
- Their channels for the publish step

name: SEO sweep and article engine
oneLiner: Scores every page, rewrites metadata for review, writes articles against a keyword map.
problem: The website ranks for nothing, nobody knows which page is weak, and content for search never gets written.
solution: A sweep audits every route (scores, findings by severity), proposes title/meta rewrites that a person approves before they ship, keeps a keyword map of terms worth owning, and an article engine writes drafts against unclaimed keywords — briefs that already have an article are never rewritten. Publishing pushes approved metadata to the live site.
payload:
# SEO sweep — build spec

1. AUDIT: crawl own routes; score per page; findings tagged severity; only pages that answered count toward the site score.
2. REWRITE: sweep drafts title/meta changes into a review queue; human approves; approved metadata deploys to the site.
3. KEYWORDS: maintain a map of terms worth owning + who currently owns them; unclaimed terms feed the article queue.
4. ARTICLES: writer takes brief → draft → same review gate; skip briefs that already produced an article.
5. VERIFY: scheduled GSC check closes the loop on what actually moved.

## Adapt per client
- Their stack's deploy hook for metadata
- Keyword seeds from their niche + competitors

name: Outbound email sequencer
oneLiner: Multi-step outbound that researches, drafts in voice, sends on schedule, and stops itself.
problem: Founders start outbound sequences by hand, forget step 2, and follow-ups die.
solution: Enrol a prospect → research pass builds context → per-step drafts written in the sender's voice and held to the voice gate → scheduled sends with a hard brake (suppression list, unsubscribe honoured, ledger that reports the truth about which day). Replies land back in the console; a reply stops the sequence.
payload:
# Outbound sequencer — build spec

1. ENROL: prospect + sequence choice; research pass gathers site/LinkedIn context into a brief.
2. DRAFT: every step drafted up front in sender's voice, through the same deterministic voice gate as content; human approves the sequence once.
3. SEND: scheduler with per-day caps; suppression list checked at send time, not enrol time; unsubscribe link honoured immediately and logged.
4. REPLY: webhook lands replies in the console; any reply halts remaining steps; founder answers personally.
5. LEDGER: what was sent, to whom, which day — the ledger must never lie about scheduling drift.

## Pins
- A brake switch that stops everything at once.
- Never fake a personal tone the founder cannot sustain in the reply.

## Adapt per client
- Sender voice session → gate rules
- Their CRM as enrolment source

name: AI Discovery Sprint
oneLiner: Two days on-site, twelve interviews, a scored top-5 and a report that is the proposal.
problem: SMB clients know automation should save them time but cannot say where; pitches without a measured baseline are just opinions, and the proposal that follows gets haggled like one.
solution: A fixed-price, fixed-shape engagement. Prep week builds a roster, one shared field card and a prep brief per person. Two interview days on-site: 45-minute slots, live whisper capture, the same three baseline questions every session (what repeats weekly, how long does it take, what would you do with the time back). Synthesis turns transcripts into per-person needs, scores every candidate tool on a weighted rubric (time 30%, cash 25%, errors 20%, feasibility 15%, future-proof 10%) and keeps the top 5. The deliverable is one report — quotes, flowcharts, baseline table — with the fixed-price proposal built in as the last chapter. Ran at Durabo: 12 sessions, 2 days, ±80–100 repetitive hours/week surfaced across ~20 staff.
payload:
# AI Discovery Sprint — build spec

## Shape

### Prep (the week before)
1. Roster: who we interview, which day, which slot — sourced from the client's own scheduling truth, not a sheet we invent. 45-min slots with buffer between.
2. Field card: one interview script for everyone. The interviewer ticks it live; unticked steps feed the mid-interview insight pass.
3. Prep brief per person: role, systems they touch, what we already suspect repeats. Written before day one, corrected during.

### Interview days (2 days on-site)
4. Live capture (see bp-seed-interview-capture): phone records, whisper transcribes live, transcript grows on both founders' phones, insight pass on demand.
5. Every session asks the baseline three: what repeats weekly, how long does it take, what would you do with the time back. Everything else is role-specific; these three never get skipped.

### Synthesis
6. Per-person needs list, pulled from transcripts, not from memory.
7. Rubric scoring: time saved 30% · cash impact 25% · error reduction 20% · feasibility 15% · future-proof 10%. Score every candidate tool, keep the top 5, show the scores.
8. Report: verbatim quotes, flowcharts of the current processes, and the baseline table — hours per person per week, marked self-reported or clocked.

### Delivery
9. The report IS the proposal. Fixed price for the top-5 build sits in the last chapter. No separate sales deck; the evidence sells or nothing does.

## Pins
- Group interviews confuse transcripts — record who is in the room, every session, before the first question.
- Baseline numbers must be self-reported AND clocked where possible; the report says which is which.
- Quotes verbatim from raw transcripts, never from summaries. A summary's quote is a paraphrase wearing quotation marks.

## Adapt per client
- Language: interviews and report in theirs.
- Roster source: whatever holds their scheduling truth.
- Rubric weights: a cash-tight client weighs cash heavier; a compliance-heavy one weighs errors.
